base_clip_s01.notes: Reproduces Phase 30 s01 (same frames to the eye): opens eyes, hands shift slightly; 'sways gently' barely visible; 'slow push-in' not performed (zoom 0.98).

A1_s1.notes: Walks steadily toward camera, grows in frame, gait implied by skirt/shoulder motion (feet hidden by lehenga). Background arches also enlarge slightly (some implicit camera advance).

A2_s1.notes: Same as W1; descriptive wording adds a little arm swing; no visible gain over W1.

B1_s1.notes: Clean continuous 180-degree turn front -> back, dupatta drapes plausibly. Back view: long jasmine braid is gone (hair reads as pinned up). Ends on her back (usable as a turn-away beat).

B2_s1.notes: Near-identical trajectory to B1 (same seed): turns to a back view; the second clause 'looks back over her shoulder at the camera' is NOT performed. Dupatta turns from opaque silk to a sheer veil in the back view.

C1_s1.notes: Arms go out to the sides, then up overhead and are held; face visible throughout; bangles stay on. Hands small and soft at 704x1280.

C2_s1.notes: Reads as a classical gesture (hands to chest, open palms near the face, arms rising), smaller than C1. Hands are the subject and are soft/blobby at 704x1280 - weak as a hero shot.

D1_s1.notes: Gentle head tilt and slight lean; very stable, but the sway is subtle (centre energy 4.2 vs 7-12 for walking/turning). Usable as a calm verse shot, not as a rhythmic beat shot.

D2_s1.notes: Same as D1 with a little more head movement and a smile; descriptive wording adds almost nothing measurable (centre energy 4.4 vs 4.2).

E1_s1.notes: Near-full rotation front -> side -> back -> three-quarter front, skirt begins to flare at the end; face returns recognisable.

E2_s1.notes: Partial turn with a large, physically plausible skirt flare and flowing dupatta; face visible most of the clip. Descriptive wording ('skirt flaring softly') measurably changed the result (more flare, edge/centre 0.24 vs 0.12).

F1_s1.notes: Generic 'performs to the music' yields only small hand movements near the chest (centre energy 3.6). Not a performance shot.

F2_s1.notes: All three clauses performed: steps forward, sinks into a deep bend, rises with open arms; skirt pools/folds plausibly; spread fingers soft. Concrete physical verbs (step/bend/rise) executed where 'performs' (F1) was not.

G1_s1.notes: 'she dances' -> upper-body hand gestures at chest/shoulder height, body stationary; no steps. Calm, stable, but reads as gesturing, not dancing.

G2_s1.notes: Mudra-like hand gestures near the chest; 'small steps' not performed; lowest energy of the dance prompts (centre 3.9). Descriptive wording did not add footwork.

H1_s1.notes: Livelier arm work than G (centre 5.7), slight torso lean, one arm raised at the end; feet/body stay in place. Reads as an arm dance, not 'energetic dance'.

H2_s1.notes: Sweeping arms rising overhead (centre 6.8, highest of the dance prompts so far); 'rhythmic steps' not performed. Usable with selection as an in-place dance beat.

I1_s1.notes: 'fast energetic dance' -> moderate-pace arm gestures at chest height, slight body turn; centre energy 5.9 = same as medium dance (H1 5.7). The model does not produce fast movement; result is indistinguishable from H.

I2_s1.notes: Genuine energetic dance: body rotates, skirt swirls wide, sharp arm accents; centre energy 12.2 = 2x I1. Footwork hidden by the skirt; hands/arms blur at speed. Descriptive wording made the decisive difference vs I1. Single seed -> needs the repeat test and real-time viewing.

J1_s1.notes: 'she jumps' -> she shifts weight and drifts toward the camera; never airborne (Phase 30 leap failure reproduced).

J2_s1.notes: Descriptive leap wording -> namaste-like hand gesture and a slight dip; never airborne. Leap/jump fails with both wordings (and in Phase 30).

K1_s1.notes: 'slow push-in': zoom first->last 1.02 (no visible push); she stands and smiles. As a static smile shot it is clean (would be 3-4), but the requested camera move did not happen.

K2_s1.notes: Push-in executed: gradual dolly from full body to waist-up, face grows, background enlarges (edge/centre 0.66). Explicit camera-verb wording ('the camera slowly dollies forward toward her face') worked where the short 'slow push-in' (K1) did not. zoom metric misreads this off-centre push (0.92).

L1_s1.notes: She turns to profile and walks left while the framing follows her and the background slides (edge/centre 0.67); reads as a close follow shot. Face in profile (identity weaker). Whether it reads as camera tracking vs. subject turning needs real-time viewing.

L2_s1.notes: Near-identical to L1 (same seed): profile walk to the left, framing follows and drifts closer; at the end her face approaches the frame edge. Explicit lateral wording added nothing measurable (edge/centre 0.66 vs 0.67).

M1_s1.notes: 'camera orbits around her' -> nearly a still frame (energy 1.28, no parallax). Same as Phase 30 (orbit 1/5).

M2_s1.notes: Descriptive orbit wording ('slow cinematic arc ... background rotating behind her') -> still frame (energy 1.49). Orbit fails with both wordings.

N1_s1.failures: FACE_DRIFT (with strong expression); HAND_ARTIFACT (foreshortened hand near lens)
N1_s1.notes: Expressive singing: open-mouth vowels, head movement, a hand reaching toward the lens. Face widens/softens versus the keyframe once the expression is strong (Phase 30 close-up finding reproduced); large foreshortened hand in the foreground.

N2_s1.failures: HAND_ARTIFACT (fist occludes the face ~1/3 of the clip); FACE_DRIFT
N2_s1.notes: Both clauses performed (sings, then smiles warmly - the smile at the end is the best close-up moment so far). But a large fist rises in front of the face mid-clip. Both close-up wordings contain 'toward the camera' and both produce a hand reaching at the lens -> hypothesis tested in stage 2 (N3 without it).

X1_s1.failures: COSTUME_DRIFT (dupatta becomes sheer in back view); MOTION_TOO_WEAK (arms)
X1_s1.notes: 2 concepts: the turn is performed (front -> back), the 'flowing arm movements' are small. Dupatta turns into a translucent veil in the back view, as in B2 - a repeatable back-view costume drift.

X2_s1.notes: 3 concepts performed IN ORDER: slight sway, both arms raised above the head and held, smile. Sequential composition of simple motions works.

X3_s1.notes: Overloaded prompt does NOT break the clip: the model keeps what it can do (energetic in-place dance, arm flourishes, skirt swirl - like I2, centre energy 13.4) and silently drops the spin, jump, orbit and zoom. Risk is not artifacts but unfulfilled instructions.

Y1_s1.notes: Turning (B2 text) + 'slow push-in': practically identical to B2 (centre energy 9.8 vs 9.9). Short camera text neither moved the camera nor changed or degraded the subject motion.

Y2_s1.notes: Sway (D2 text) + 'slow push-in': same as D2; no push.

A1_s2.notes: Repeat (seed 31002): walks toward the camera and grows in frame, same quality as A1_s1.

B1_s2.notes: Repeat: full turn to a back view; this time the jasmine braid stays visible and the dupatta stays opaque - the B1_s1 braid loss was seed-dependent.

C1_s2.notes: Repeat: arms out then overhead and held - nearly the same trajectory as C1_s1.

E2_s2.notes: Repeat: spin with a very wide, dramatic lehenga flare filling the frame width - exaggerated but reads as a classic twirl; face recognisable throughout.

F2_s2.notes: Repeat: step forward, deep bend, rise with open arms - all three clauses again (centre energy 9.8).

K2_s2.notes: Repeat: explicit push-in executed again (full body -> three-quarter, face enlarges; edge/centre 0.76). The explicit camera sentence is repeatable with a still subject.

I2_s2.notes: Repeat: energetic dance again - rotation, skirt swirl, sharp arm accents (centre 13.8). Executed 2/2 with the descriptive wording. Fast-motion artifacts (hand morphing, blur) can hide between the 12 sampled frames -> real-time viewing required before promotion.

L1_s2.notes: Repeat: subject turns to profile and walks left, partly out of frame at the end - the camera does NOT follow this time. Tracking 1/2 seeds.

N3_s1.notes: New wording without 'toward the camera' + 'hands out of frame': sings, then smiles/laughs; NO hand occlusion. Framing drifts down (shift y 37 px); face widens with the laugh.

N3_s2.notes: Same wording, seed 31002: clear singing mouth shapes, warm smile, steady framing, hands out of frame, identity holds. Close-up fixed by wording (2/2).

mp_01.failures: LIGHTING_JUMP (minor, luma jump 3.5 in the first frames)
mp_01.notes: New scene (oil-lamp courtyard at dusk): explicit push-in executed - full body to three-quarter, warm smile. 3/3 for the explicit push-in sentence with a still subject.

mp_02.notes: New scene (colonnade): walks toward the camera, grows from small to three-quarter; identity holds.

mp_03.notes: New scene (misty rooftop): arms curve up and are held overhead; same trajectory family as C1 s1/s2.

mp_04.notes: New scene (marble hall): turn to a back view; the dupatta again becomes a translucent veil when seen from behind (4 of the 7 turning clips that reach a back view) - a known turning artifact, not a blocker.

mp_05.failures: FACE_DRIFT (broad laugh); HAND_ARTIFACT (hand briefly at the lower frame edge)
mp_05.notes: New scene (oil-lamp temple steps at night): sings, then laughs and smiles; face rounds out with the laugh but stays recognisable; a hand flashes at the bottom-left edge for ~0.3 s (no occlusion of the face).

mp_06.notes: New scene (sunrise rooftop, backlit): spin to a side/back view with a wide skirt flare; face three-quarter at the end.

mp_07.notes: New scene (festival lights, crowd behind): steps forward, sinks low, rises with open arms - 3/3 for the step/bend/rise wording.

mp_08.notes: New scene (golden grass at sunrise): arms out and overhead, held; strong backlight flare flickers as arms pass the sun.

mp_09.notes: New scene (lotus pond at dawn): plain 'she spins' -> turn to the back and round again with the dupatta flying; braid and costume hold.

mp_10.failures: MOTION_TOO_WEAK (barely walks); LIGHTING_JUMP (firework flash, luma jump 8.5)
mp_10.notes: New scene (rooftop at night with fireworks): she barely moves forward; the fireworks animate. First walking miss (walking 4/5). Bright animated backgrounds may compete with subject motion - single observation.

ml_06.failures: MOTION_TOO_WEAK (partial turn); LIGHTING_JUMP (backlit sun, luma jump 7.0)
ml_06.notes: 16:9 counterpart of mp_06: partial turn with a moderate flare (portrait: full spin, wide flare). Subject smaller in frame; face tiny at full-body framing.

ml_07.failures: FACE_DRIFT (face slightly longer than reference); LIGHTING_JUMP (luma jump 5.0)
ml_07.notes: 16:9 counterpart of mp_07: steps, sinks low, rises with open arms (executed); framing tightens during the clip; festival setting reads cinematic in landscape.

ml_08.notes: 16:9 counterpart of mp_08: arms raised overhead and held; small figure in a wide golden field - strong composition, small face.

ml_09.notes: 16:9 counterpart of mp_09: turns to a side view and looks back over her shoulder with a dupatta swirl (portrait: full turn). Face recognisable.

ml_10.notes: 16:9 counterpart of mp_10: drifts toward the camera and to the right (shift x 48 px) rather than a clear walk; fireworks animate. Both fireworks clips are the weakest walking shots.

Y3_s1.notes: Turning (B2 text) + EXPLICIT push-in sentence: the camera dollies in to waist-up WHILE she turns, and she looks back over her shoulder (never performed in B2/Y1); dupatta stays opaque. The explicit camera sentence does not degrade subject motion (1 sample).
